title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Comprehensive Templates and Runbooks
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard on-call processes, runbook templates, postmortem format, rotation management, game day guidance, and status page / customer communications templates. It is a reference for SREs, Platform engineers, support, and anyone designated as an incident commander (IC). Keep this page current; changes to SLOs, pager policies, or escalation contacts must be reflected within 24 hours of approval.

Table of contents:
1) Incident lifecycle and ownership
2) Pager and severity definitions
3) Runbook templates (service-level and component-level)
4) Incident commander playbook (IC checklist)
5) Postmortem template and timeline
6) On-call rotations and handover checklist
7) Game day exercises and sample scenarios
8) Status page and customer communication templates
9) Metrics, SLOs, and alert thresholds
10) Appendix: contacts, tooling, and links

1) Incident lifecycle and ownership
- Goal: Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to resolve (MTTR) while preserving safety and customer communication SLA.
- Owners and roles:
  - Pager: person who receives the initial alert (primary on-call).
  - Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination and communications for the incident.
  - Tech Lead / Escalation Owner: subject matter expert for the implicated service.
  - Communications Lead: owns external and internal status updates.
  - Postmortem Author: documents the root cause, timeline, and follow-ups.
- Escalation windows and responsibilities are defined per-service in the service inventory (see Appendix links).

2) Pager and severity definitions
- Severity levels (applied consistently across Platform and Serving runtime):
  - Sev 1 (P0): Complete outage or severe degradation of customer-facing functionality affecting >30% of customers or business-critical SLAs. Pager to on-call, notify leadership (Engineering Director + Head of SRE). Target: MTTA < 5 min; MTTR as required.
  - Sev 2 (P1): Partial outage or severe degradation affecting a subset of customers or major internal systems (e.g., model serving latency > 400ms 99th percentile). Pager to on-call with escalation to Tech Lead within 15 minutes.
  - Sev 3 (P2): Degraded behavior that impacts non-critical workflows or non-customer-facing infra. Handled during business hours by on-call rotation.
  - Sev 4 (P3): Informational or low-impact issues; ticketed for triage.
- Immediate actions on pager receive:
  1. Acknowledge within 5 minutes for Sev1, 15 minutes for Sev2, 1 business hour for Sev3.
  2. If not acknowledged in the window, automatic escalation to next on-call and paging to manager.

3) Runbook templates
- Use a single canonical runbook per service (service-runbooks stored in service inventory). Each runbook should follow this template:

Service runbook header:
- service_name: (short name, e.g., serving-runtime-kvcache)
- owner_team: (team)
- primary_oncall_slack: (channel)
- pager_channel: (PagerDuty policy or Opsgenie)
- runbook_last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD

Indicator & triage steps:
1) Symptoms: (clear bullet list of user-visible symptoms and monitoring signals)
2) Primary dashboards & query examples:
   - Grafana: Redwood / Serving / latency (panel links)
   - Log query: "level:ERROR AND service:serving-runtime" (ELK/Kibana sample)
3) Quick checks (run in order):
   a) Check cluster health: `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide`
   b) Check queue depth / backpressure: `redis-cli --stat` or `curl https://metrics.internal/api/queues`
   c) Verify model-serving nodes reachable: `nc -vz <node-ip> 8080`

Mitigation & rollback steps:
- Mitigation 1: Restart model-serving worker (use rolling restart):
  1. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-worker -n serving`
  2. Monitor pods: `kubectl get pods -n serving -w`
- Mitigation 2: Route traffic to fallback model variant (policy-based routing):
  1. Update routing config: `redwoodctl routing set --service serving-runtime --variant cpu-fallback --weight 100`
  2. Validate: `redwoodctl routing get --service serving-runtime`
- If rollback required (deploy or config change):
  1. Identify last known good revision: `kubectl rollout history deployment/serving-api -n serving`
  2. Roll back: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/serving-api --to-revision=<rev>`

Post-fix validation:
- Validate real traffic: run smoke test against production canary endpoint: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"smoke test"}'`
- Check SLO metrics: 99th percentile latency, error rate, and system CPU/GPU utilization.

4) Incident commander (IC) checklist (playbook)
Initial 0-15 minutes:
1. Confirm severity and scope (samples of affected customers, regions).
2. Create incident channel (Slack) and ticket in Jira/Incident Tracker with standardized prefix: INCIDENT-[YYYYMMDD]-<service>-<shortdesc>.
3. Assign roles: IC, Communications Lead, Scribe, Tech Leads.
4. Determine immediate mitigation (based on runbook).

15-60 minutes:
1. Execute mitigation steps.
2. Provide an update in incident channel and post initial status to internal status dashboard.
3. If Sev1/Sev2, prepare public status page message (see templates below).

60+ minutes:
1. If unresolved after 60 minutes, escalate to on-call manager and schedule a war room with execs as needed.
2. Continue timed updates every 30 minutes until service recovery.

Incident close criteria:
- Service metrics returned to baseline for at least two metric windows (configurable per-service, default 15 minutes).
- Customer-impacting errors resolved, and follow-up ticket(s) created for root-cause fixes.

5) Postmortem template and timeline
- Target: publish a postmortem within 72 hours of incident close; final postmortem with action items due within 14 days.
- Postmortem fields (flat):
  - title: string
  - incident_id: string (e.g., INCIDENT-20260202-serving-latency)
  - severity: Sev1/Sev2/etc.
  - start_time: YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm UTC
  - end_time: YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm UTC
  - detection: how the incident was detected (alert, customer, automated test)
  - timeline: bullet list of timestamped events (UTC)
  - root_cause: summary sentence
  - contributing_factors: bullet list
  - mitigations_taken: bullet list
  - action_items: numbered list with owner and due_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
  - postmortem_author: name
  - reviewers: list of names
  - related_incidents: list of incident_ids

Example timeline snippet:
- 2026-01-30 14:05 UTC: Pager fired for high 99th percentile latency on serving-runtime (Grafana alert ID: SRV-LAT-99-ALERT).
- 2026-01-30 14:07 UTC: Primary on-call acknowledged; IC created INCIDENT-20260130-serving-latency.
- 2026-01-30 14:20 UTC: Discovered increased KV cache eviction causing model cold starts.
- 2026-01-30 14:35 UTC: Rolled traffic to cpu-fallback variants.
- 2026-01-30 15:05 UTC: Metrics returned to baseline.

6) On-call rotations and handover checklist
- Rotation model: 1-week primary on-call, 2-week secondary (follow-the-sun optional for APAC coverage). Standard shifts start Monday 09:00 UTC.
- Handover checklist (to be posted to Slack #oncall-handover channel):
  1. Current pager status and open alerts/tickets (link to incident tickets).
  2. Outstanding action items and owners.
  3. Any ongoing mitigations and rollback windows.
  4. Scheduled maintenance or deploys that overlap the shift.
  5. Quick health check results (dashboard screenshots or links).
- Coverage rules:
  - Primary should not take lengthy time-off during on-call week. If needed, swap with backup and update PagerDuty.
  - For holidays or extended absences, contact oncall-manager@redwood.com to assign temporary coverage.

7) Game days (exercise program)
- Purpose: validate runbooks, tooling, alert fidelity, and team coordination.
- Cadence: Quarterly platform-level game day; team-level monthly or bi-monthly smaller exercises.
- Typical scenario example (30-90 minute exercise):
  Scenario: KV cache eviction causes >50% request latency increase for serving-runtime in us-west-2.
  Objectives:
   1. Verify alert triggers and on-call acknowledgement flow.
   2. Execute runbook mitigations (routing to fallback variant).
   3. Post-exercise: measure MTTA and MTTR, collect feedback, and update runbook.
- Scoring: measure time to detect, acknowledge, mitigate, and restore. Document lessons and required follow-ups in a short retro.

8) Status page and customer communications templates
- Internal policy: Publish to internal status page within 30 minutes of confirmed impact for Sev1; public status page update within 60 minutes if customers are affected.
- Public status page template (short):
  Title: Service Degradation: <service> (region)
  Impact: Brief description of affected functionality and customer impact.
  Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Resolved
  Started: YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm UTC
  Next update: In 30 minutes or when status changes
  Contact: support@redwood.com or support portal link

  Example:
  Title: Service Degradation: Redwood Serving (us-west-2)
  Impact: Generation requests experienced elevated latencies and timeouts for ~40% of requests.
  Status: Mitigating
  Started: 2026-01-30 14:05 UTC
  Next update: 2026-01-30 14:35 UTC

- Customer email / public message template (use short, non-technical language):
  Subject: Partial outage affecting Redwood inference in us-west-2

  Hi <customer name>,

  We are investigating an issue affecting inference requests in us-west-2. Some requests may experience elevated latency or timeouts. Our team has identified a mitigation and is routing traffic to a fallback model variant to restore service. We will send updates every 30 minutes until resolved.

  We apologize for the disruption. If you need immediate assistance, please contact support@redwood.com.

9) Metrics, SLOs, and alert thresholds
- Example SLOs (per-customer, service-level defaults):
  - Availability SLO: 99.95% per calendar month (target for Redwood API hosted endpoints).
  - Latency SLO: 99th percentile tail latency < 350ms (generation endpoints, 1-2k token prompts).
  - Error Rate: < 0.25% 5xx errors per 10-minute window.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Sev1: 5xx error rate > 1% over 5 minutes AND customer impact > 5 customers.
  - Sev2: 99th percentile latency > 450ms over 10 minutes.
  - Sev3: Queue depth > 500 for more than 5 minutes.
- Dashboards to check: Serving / Throughput, Serving / Latency, Serving / Errors, GPU Utilization, KV Cache Hit Rate.

10) Appendix: contacts, tooling, and links
- Oncall & Escalation Slack channels: #oncall, #oncall-handover, #incidents
- Pager: PagerDuty policy: Redwood-Platform-Oncall (link in internal tools)
- Incident Tracker: Jira project RED-INC
- Runbook repo: git@repo.redwood.com:runbooks/service-runbooks.git
- Postmortem storage: Confluence page under /postmortems
- Key contacts:
  - Oncall Manager: Marcus Lee (marcus.lee@redwood.com)
  - Head of SRE: Priya Rao (priya.rao@redwood.com)
  - Support escalation: support-escalations@redwood.com

Change control and ownership:
- This document is owned by the Engineering team (On-call & Incident Response subteam). Reviewer group: SRE, Platform, and Developer Experience.
- All changes must be peer reviewed and published with an updated last_reviewed date.

Quick links (examples):
- Service inventory: confluence/eng-platform/service-inventory
- SLO policy: confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets-2025
- Pager and escalation config: internal PagerDuty dashboard

End of playbook.
